title: FBI Hunts Indian National Harmanveer Singh in Canada-Linked Drug Trafficking Crackdown
excerpt: Singh, 31, is wanted for allegedly managing narcotics operations for the Ravinder Dhanda crime syndicate as part of Operation Hard Ball, which has led to 24 arrests and 37 indictments across the U.S., Canada, and Europe.
body:
• The FBI has issued a federal arrest warrant for Harmanveer Singh, 31, over his alleged role in the Ravinder Dhanda drug trafficking network operating across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico.
  • Operation Hard Ball, a joint U.S.-Canada-Europe crackdown, has targeted three India-based crime syndicates — the Lawrence Bishnoi Gang, the Dhanda network, and the Bhagwanpuria gang — resulting in 24 arrests and 37 indictments.
  • Law enforcement has seized approximately 1,000 kilograms of cocaine, a kilogram of heroin, $40,000 in cash, and a dozen firearms across the investigation.
  • The FBI has also announced a $50,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of Goldy Brar, the North American leader of the Bishnoi enterprise.

A Fugitive in a Transnational Drug Network

The Federal Bureau of Investigation is searching for Harmanveer Singh, a 31-year-old Indian national, over his alleged involvement in a transnational drug trafficking operation tied to a Canada-based crime syndicate, the agency announced this week.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Da5RnYImlBS/

Singh, who also uses the aliases "Hari Gautam" and "Harman Sandhu," allegedly managed narcotics trafficking operations for the Ravinder Dhanda Organised Crime Group, according to the FBI. The Dhanda network is accused of moving large shipments of cocaine and methamphetamine across trafficking routes spanning the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

A federal arrest warrant was issued for Singh by the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California on June 23, 2026. He faces charges of conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute controlled substances, conspiracy to export controlled substances, and possession with intent to distribute, according to federal court records.

Operation Hard Ball: A Sweeping International Crackdown

Singh's case is part of a broader law enforcement operation codenamed "Operation Hard Ball" — a joint international effort targeting transnational organised crime networks originating from India, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

https://x.com/FBILosAngeles/status/2080009540393746767

The operation focused on three major syndicates: the Lawrence Bishnoi Gang, the Ravinder Dhanda network, and the Bhagwanpuria gang. Together, the crackdown has resulted in 24 arrests and 37 indictments across the United States, with arrests also made in Canada, Spain, and other parts of Europe.

"Transnational criminal gangs who spread fear, drugs, and violence will face the full force of justice and the weight of the federal government."

— Bill Essayli, First Assistant United States Attorney

Law enforcement has seized approximately 1,000 kilograms of cocaine and one kilogram of heroin, along with $40,000 in cash and a dozen firearms. A total of 34 search warrants have been executed across the Sacramento and Los Angeles areas.

The Bishnoi Connection and Nijjar Assassination

The indictments unsealed as part of Operation Hard Ball extend far beyond drug trafficking. Lawrence Bishnoi, 33, a gangster imprisoned in India, has been charged alongside his lieutenant Satinderjeet Singh, known as "Goldy Brar," with ordering the June 2023 assassination of Hardeep Singh Nijjar — a prominent Sikh separatist leader who was gunned down outside a gurdwara in Surrey, British Columbia.

According to the Justice Department, Bishnoi ran a sweeping criminal enterprise from his prison cell using contraband cellphones, personally directing assassinations, extortions, kidnappings, and drug trafficking operations across multiple continents. The Canadian government designated the Bishnoi enterprise as a terrorist entity in September 2025.

The FBI has announced a $50,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of Goldy Brar, described as the North American leader of the Bishnoi enterprise. Ten fugitives remain at large — seven in the United States, two in India, and one in Europe.

A Web of Violence and Extortion

The three indictments paint a picture of criminal networks that have operated with impunity across borders for years. The Dhanda network alone is accused of transporting hundreds of kilograms of cocaine and methamphetamine weekly from the U.S. into Canada, using long-haul semi-trucks and even farm vehicles to conceal shipments.

The Bhagwanpuria gang, led by Jaggu Bhagwanpuria from prison in India, allegedly boasts more than 1,000 members and associates worldwide, including over 100 in the United States. Members have been charged with murder-for-hire, weapons trafficking, and corrupting law enforcement officers in India.

Impact on the Indian Diaspora

The Justice Department specifically noted that the impact of these criminal networks "is especially felt in the Indian diaspora." The syndicates have been accused of targeting prominent religious, social, and political leaders within diaspora communities, using high-profile acts of violence to terrorise and extort victims.

Extortion attempts have targeted individuals across California and the Midwest, with one defendant allegedly threatening to "put bullets in your kids" while in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody, according to court documents.

As the manhunt for Singh and nine other fugitives continues, the case underscores the growing reach of India-based criminal networks into North American communities — and the intensifying international effort to dismantle them.
